summary: Centralized temporary Slack channel provisioning with timebound approvals and automatic Confluence runbook linkback
description:
Issue summary: Request to create an automated, auditable workflow for creating temporary Slack channels for cross-pod experiments and oncall handovers. The workflow should: 1) provision a channel with standardized naming and pinned meta message; 2) open a Confluence runbook stub populated from a blueprint and link it into the channel; 3) require a timebound approval from the pod lead (via Slack or Jira) for channels >48 hours; 4) auto-archive channels at TTL expiration and record archive metadata in Confluence.

Impact: Current ad-hoc channel creation leads to noise, orphaned channels, and fragmented runbooks. This causes discoverability problems for incident follow-ups and long-term knowledge capture. Owners report extra manual steps to enforce retention and approvals.

Requested deliverables:
- Slack provisioning automation (bot/shortcut) that enforces name template: tmp-<pod>-<purpose>-<YYYYMMDD>.
- Integration to create Confluence page from 'temporary-channel-runbook' blueprint and post the link as the first pinned message.
- Approval flow: for channels requested >48 hours, send an approval to the nominated pod lead; allow approve/reject from Slack or Jira comment.
- TTL enforcement: default 7 days, configurable on request; auto-archive at TTL expiry and append archive metadata to the Confluence stub.
- Audit trail: store channel metadata (creator, created_at, approver, TTL, archive_ts) into a central Confluence table and emit an event to #infra-audit.

Acceptance criteria:
- Non-admin users can request temporary channels via Slack shortcut or Jira portal.
- Channels created by automation follow naming and have Confluence link pinned within 2 minutes.
- Approval requests appear to the correct pod lead and expire after 24 hours if not acted on (automatically rejected).
- TTL auto-archive works in a test workspace and metadata is persisted to Confluence.
- Documentation: runbook for operations and a short runbook for pod leads on approval behavior.

Timeline: prototype in staging by 2026-03-24, pilot with two pods for 2 weeks, GA rollout after pilot and security review.
comments: 2026-03-10 - Maya Chen: Filing request after multiple pods reported orphaned channels next to the model-eval pilot. Added acceptance criteria and suggested timeline.

2026-03-11 - Rafael Ortega: Reviewed scope. Suggest using the existing infra-bot framework and extending the confluence-client module rather than building new service. Need security review for Confluence write access. Assigned to myself to draft an implementation plan.

2026-03-11 - Priya Singh (Security): Flagging that the bot must use scoped API token with least privilege. Also request a design doc for audit storage and retention policy. We can approve test Confluence write scope for staging only.

2026-03-12 - Rafael Ortega: Implementation plan uploaded to GitHub (see related PR). Plan includes Slack shortcut -> GitHub action -> infra-bot lambda -> Confluence page creation -> channel pin. Awaiting security token provisioning and a code review.
2026-03-12 - Ops Lead (Liam O'Connor): Pilot pods nominated: model-eval and observability. Confirmed pod leads for approval flow: @anna-platform, @samer-sre.
investigation_notes: Checked slack provisioning patterns used by ephemeral workspace automation (INT-117263) and found reusable name-template validation code in infra-bots repo.
Confluence blueprint exists (temporary-channel-runbook) but lacks metadata fields for TTL and approver; will extend blueprint with fields: ttl_days, approver, created_by, created_at, archive_ts.
Audit event pipeline: proposal to emit structured event to #infra-audit and store one-line JSON in Confluence append-only table. Need input from legal on retention (requested).
Potential blockers: Scoped KMS/KV for bot tokens for Confluence and a small IAM change to enable app-managed page creation. Security has requested a design review meeting.

Performance considerations: creating pages at channel creation should be async-with-retry and not block user experience; fallback behavior: channel gets created and bot posts placeholder message linking to 'runbook creation pending'.
resolution_notes: 2026-03-12 - Rafael Ortega: Created feature branch and initial PR to extend infra-bots with a 'tmp-channel' flow. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-bots/pull/812. Prototype uses staged Confluence token and Slack app modal for TTL selection.
Temporary mitigation: added a short playbook for on-call to manually create standardized channels and Confluence stubs until automation is live (link in Confluence).
Next steps: schedule security design review (action assigned to Priya), provision staging Confluence token, and run pilot with two pods. Will update ticket with pilot results and GA checklist.
